tip_title: Before Your Policy Renews, There Are a Few Add-Ons Worth Actually Knowing About
topic: Home Insurance - Endorsements and Optional Add-Ons
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: Before Your Policy Renews, There Are a Few Add-Ons Worth Actually Knowing About**

Standard homeowners policies have real gaps — and most insurers offer optional endorsements to fill them, but nobody calls you up and explains that. Sewer and drain backup coverage is one that catches people off guard regularly: standard policies exclude it, but the damage from a backed-up line can be extensive and the endorsement to add it is typically pretty affordable. Equipment breakdown coverage is another one worth knowing about — it covers major home systems like your HVAC or water heater when they fail mechanically, which standard policies don't touch. And if you've added anything valuable to your home or bought new gear over the last year, an extended personal property endorsement might be worth a look. None of these are automatic. You have to ask.

Not sure which endorsements your current policy has — or what's missing? Your Peachy agent can pull up your declarations page and walk through the options.

📖 [Learn more from U.S. News](https://www.usnews.com/insurance/homeowners-insurance/how-to-buy-homeowners-insurance)

This tip narrows to three specific endorsements with concrete descriptions of what each one does and doesn't cover, framed as a pre-renewal action item. tip_title: Still Paying Off Your Car? One Question Worth Asking Before the End of the Year.
topic: Auto Insurance - Gap Insurance Periodic Review
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: Still Paying Off Your Car? One Question Worth Asking Before the End of the Year.**

Gap insurance exists to cover the difference between what your car is worth and what you still owe on the loan if the car gets totaled. That gap is biggest in the first year or two after purchase, when depreciation is steepest and your loan balance is still high. But here's the thing — a lot of people keep paying for gap insurance long after they've crossed over and their car's value is actually higher than what they owe. If you've had your car for a few years, made a solid down payment, or have been paying ahead on the loan, you may not be underwater anymore. It takes about five minutes to check: look up a current market value estimate for your vehicle and compare it to your loan payoff amount.

Not sure if gap coverage still makes sense for your situation? Your Peachy agent can walk through the numbers with you.

📖 [Learn more from Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/articles/personal-finance/102914/do-drivers-really-need-gap-insurance.asp)
summary: Covers gap insurance as a periodic review item for existing policyholders who may no longer be upside down on their loan, framed as an end-of-year check rather than a purchase decision or coverage exclusion angle.
scoring_notes: Prior gap tips covered 'when you need it' (Aug 10) and 'what it doesn't cover' (May 8). This angle focuses specifically on whether your current loan-to-value ratio still justifies keeping the coverage — a practical year-end financial review framing. Both audiences skew toward financed vehicles (income brackets and age ranges support this).
